docs.title: Pewter developer docs
docs.text:
Pewter, by Omega Compute, is an orchestration platform for GPU capacity. Sellers list whole GPUs or supported GPU slices and connect the machine with a small agent. Buyers find capacity, agree terms, and run jobs. Everything is reachable three ways: a REST API, an MCP server for assistants and agents, and command-line tools.

Status

Pewter is in active development and the code is private. Pages marked coming soon or not yet available describe parts that are not built or not decided yet.

I want to… Start here Get something working in minutes Quickstart Rent out a GPU machine Seller flow · Seller agent Find and use capacity Buyer flow Call Pewter from Python (pewt) Python SDK (pewt) Call the API API overview Connect an assistant MCP server Understand terms Glossary · FAQ

docs.title: How the pieces fit
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  S[Seller] -->|creates listing| API[(Pewter API)]
  M[Seller machine<br/>pewter-node-agent] -->|signed heartbeats<br/>and measurements| API
  M -->|capacity proofs| E[Edge verifier]
  E -->|signed verdict| API
  B[Buyer] -->|search, deal, jobs| API
  A[Assistant / agent] -->|MCP| API

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
What does it cost? Final pricing is not yet published. Sellers set their own prices; the draft 2026-10-24.1 platform schedule ranges from 2.5% to 15% before renewal discounts, with a $5 minimum fee and $25 minimum cycle. It is not final and is subject to change — see Paying.

Is the Verified badge on? No. It is off for everyone, fail-closed, pending real-GPU validation. See Verified badge.

Which GPUs are supported? NVIDIA (whole GPUs and MIG slices with a known profile), AMD (whole GPUs only), and Apple silicon Macs. See GPU detection.

What are the rate limits? Not yet published. Limited routes answer 429 with Retry-After.

How do payments work? Not live yet; card checkout is test-mode only and escrow has only run on a testnet. See Paying.

Which regions are blocked? Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Crimea, and the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Other sanctioned programs are handled by name screening. See Regions.

Can I use it from an assistant? Yes, through the MCP server. No tool moves money.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Seller — An account that offers GPU capacity. Seller fees are seller-paid (see Paying).

Buyer — An account that searches for capacity, agrees a deal, and runs jobs on it.

Listing — A seller's offer of capacity: a capability (GPU model, count, memory, network, region, availability, price) plus a title. New listings are drafts; they go live only after the machine is measured and the listing is revalidated.

Whole GPU — A full physical device allocated to one buyer (device_class: whole, isolation whole_device).

Slice — Part of a GPU offered on its own. Today only NVIDIA MIG slices with a known profile are admitted. AMD partitions that share a driver interface are not supported, and overlapping device ranges are refused.

Machine / node — A computer running the seller agent and paired to one listing.

Pairing code — A short-lived code (XXXX-XXXX) created for a listing; the agent uses it once to register the machine.

Heartbeat — A signed message the agent sends every minute. Metering credits the time between two heartbeats for each allocated device.

Edge verifier — A standalone service that challenges the machine with a capacity proof and signs a one-use verdict that the API checks.

Proof — A challenged capacity proof: a compute check (matrix product checked with Freivalds' algorithm) and a commit-then-open memory check. See Proofs.

Verified — A badge meaning the GPU itself was proven to hold the claimed capacity. It is currently off for every machine (fail-closed). See Verified badge.

Deal — A match between a buyer and a listing. It is non-binding until both sides accept terms and any required human approval clears.

Tranche — An hourly slice of delivery used for metering, fees, holdback and payout.

Agent key — An API key with the omk_ prefix, issued to an agent on your account.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page takes you from nothing to a working connection. Buyers install the public pewter CLI and sign in against the staging API (Buyer tab). The seller agent is not published and still runs from source (Seller tab). Production API access remains invite-only.

Access

Public sign-up is coming soon. Today accounts are created by invitation (a waitlist exists at POST /api/v1/waitlist). The public CLI also requires an existing Pewter app account to approve a device login.

SellerBuyer

1. Install the agent (Node.js 22.18 or newer). This is the seller agent, not the public pewter CLI in the Buyer tab. A published package is coming soon; today the agent runs from source:

node --version            # must be >= 22.18
node src/cli.ts version   # from the pewter-node-agent source folder

2. Create a draft listing (details):

curl -X POST https://api.example/api/v1/listings/create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: my-first-listing" \
  -d @listing.json

3. Get a pairing code for that listing:

curl -X POST https://api.example/api/v1/nodes/pairings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: pair-1" \
  -d '{"listing_id": "LST-..."}'

4. Check what the agent sees (detects NVIDIA, AMD or Apple silicon GPUs):

pewter-node-agent measure

5. Connect the machine:

pewter-node-agent up --code XXXX-XXXX --api https://api.example/api/v1 --name rack-01

The agent prints Paired as NOD-… for listing LST-… and starts heartbeating. Then ask Pewter to revalidate: POST /api/v1/listings/{id}/revalidate.

Replace https://api.example with the API host you were given. The public production host is not published.

1. Install the public CLI (pewter, alias pew). v0.1.0 is read-only, talks only to the Pewter staging API, and refuses production.

On macOS (the supported Mac install; darwin binaries in 0.1.0 are not notarized):

brew trust --formula omegacomputes/tap/pewter   # Homebrew 7; required before the formula will load
brew install omegacomputes/tap/pewter

On Linux, and on macOS once OpenSSL 3 is first on PATH:

curl -fsSL https://omegacompute.com/install | sh

The curl installer verifies an Ed25519 signature on SHA256SUMS, then the SHA-256 of the archive, and installs nothing if either check fails. The release public key is in the installer, the CLI README, and https://omegacompute.com/cli/pewter-release.pub. To verify without installing:

curl -fsSLo install.sh https://omegacompute.com/install && less install.sh && sh install.sh --dry-run

Homebrew pins the same SHA-256 values, copied from that signed checksum list.

2. Sign in. Run pewter login, open the device URL it prints, enter the code, and approve the request in the Pewter app. That mints a permissioned pck_ CLI key. The key is stored locally and is never printed. The CLI refuses omk_ agent keys and session tokens.

3. Confirm:

pewter --version    # 0.1.0
pewter status       # staging host, health ok
pewter instruments  # public catalog, no key required
pewter whoami

The default API is https://pewter-staging-production.up.railway.app/api/v1. Any other host, including https://api.omegacompute.com/api/v1, is a hard error. Production is not enabled in v0.1.0. Available commands: login, logout, whoami, status, instruments, listings, orders, balance, verify, version, completion. connect is not part of this release.

4. API or MCP (optional). The public CLI uses pck_ keys. MCP and POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/keys still use engine agent keys (omk_), which the CLI will not store. See MCP.

5. Python (pewt). The package pewt is a different client from pewter / pew: a library and a pewt CLI (0.1.1). It does not log in. See Python SDK (pewt).

More detail on the public CLI is on the Buyer CLI page.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
We are preparing for an eventual open source release. For now, invited collaborators should use the repository's existing private channels or contact hello@omegacompute.com.

For a bug, include the component, version or commit, operating system, expected and actual behavior, and a minimal reproduction. Redact credentials, account details, machine identifiers, and private infrastructure. Use Security policy instead for vulnerabilities.

For feature ideas, describe the task you need to accomplish and the alternatives you have tried. Check existing issues before opening another. Public issue intake and Discussions are not launched by this draft. Support coverage and response times are not yet defined.

Website: https://omegacompute.com

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
https://api.example/api/v1

api.example is a placeholder. The production host will be published at launch.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every non-public route needs a bearer token:

Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>
Prefix What it is How you get it omk_ Agent key (for scripts, servers, agents) POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/keys — the secret is returned once and never again. GET on the same path lists prefixes and status only. pws_ Human session Signing in through the Pewter app (Apple, Google, or device-code sign-in). Some account actions require a human session and answer 403 to an agent key. pck_ Command-line session Issued by the CLI's device-code login.

Repeated failed authentication from one address is rate-limited and answers 429 with retry_after_s.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Envelope. Successful responses are wrapped as { "data": … }.

  • Errors use one shape and carry an X-Request-Id header:

    { "error": { "code": "validation_error", "message": "…", "details": null, "request_id": "…" } }

  • Idempotency. Creating or changing state requires an Idempotency-Key header (1–80 characters). Replaying the same key returns the original result instead of creating a duplicate.

  • Paging is opt-in: send limit or cursor to receive { items, next_cursor, total }; otherwise you get a plain array.
  • Rate limits. Some routes enforce per-bucket limits and answer 429 with a Retry-After header. Exact limits are not yet published.

docs.text:
This portable skill helps SI assistants explain credentials, metering and payment availability. It is guidance, not a payment service or a server-side access control.

Download the public SKILL.md

The docs site is static: key issuance happens through the authenticated API described in Overview & authentication, not on this page. For availability and draft pricing, see Paying and payouts.

docs.title: Public skill content
docs.text:
---
name: pewter-payments-keys
description: Use when connecting an SI assistant to Pewter, managing API credentials, or explaining metered compute and payment availability.
---
# Pewter payments and API keys

## Current behavior (verified)

Reviewed against developer sources on 7 November 2026. Availability depends on the approved deployment. Use `https://api.example` only as a placeholder; obtain the approved API host separately.

- Developer documentation is a static site. It explains access but does not issue credentials or process payments.
- A signed-in human owner requests an `omk_` agent key with `POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/keys`, selecting scopes. The secret is returned at creation; store it securely and never paste it into a conversation or skill file.
- `pws_` is a human session from Apple/Google sign-in. `pck_` is a CLI credential issued through device-code login approved by a human. Device-code login does not issue a human session. CLI credentials cannot mint agent keys.
- Machine measurements arrive through signed heartbeats. Device/session observations and job running/GPU-seconds contribute to metering; delivery records roll into hourly tranches. Test-network ledger values are simulated, not cash.
- Real-money metered access is not available in the audited build. Card checkout is test-mode only; internal delivery funding is sandbox-only. See the Paying and payouts documentation for availability and draft pricing.
- Claude-compatible MCP OAuth support exists in the code. Use only the approved Pewter staging connector when configured; its running connection was not verified by this source review. Connector sign-in is not a payment receipt.

## Coming soon: required payment activation

These are target requirements, not a claim that the current server implements paid activation:

- No metered key activation without a successful charge or funded credit hold.
- Server-confirmed funding and atomic job/cycle reservations before paid work starts.
- Account/per-key spend caps and idempotent usage settlement.
- Suspension of metered access on failed payment or zero available balance, with bounded stopping of active work and reconciliation before reactivation.

A skill is guidance, not server-side enforcement. Do not promise paid access before the service announces availability and the server confirms it.

## Operating safely

1. Confirm the approved environment, account and supported connection method.
2. Use least-privilege credentials and the platform's secure credential storage.
3. Keep test funds separate from real payments; never treat a browser success screen as proof of a charge.
4. Obtain explicit approval before any purchase, funding, key creation or configuration change. Loading this skill authorizes none of those actions.
5. Report current capabilities separately from coming-soon requirements. Do not invent endpoints, payment receipts or runtime status.

docs.title: Deals, orders & fees
docs.text:
A deal is a match between a buyer and a listing. It is non-binding until both sides accept terms and any required human approval clears.

Route Purpose GET/POST /orders, POST /orders/quote, POST /orders/{id}/cancel Buyer orders and quotes GET /matches, GET /needs, GET /rfqs Matching and requests GET /deals, GET /deals/{id} Deals POST /deals/{id}/terms, POST /deals/{id}/accept Agree terms GET /deals/{id}/delivery, GET /deals/{id}/tranches Delivery and hourly tranches POST /deals/{id}/jobs, GET /jobs/{id}, /jobs/{id}/logs, /jobs/{id}/artifacts, POST /jobs/{id}/cancel Run and manage jobs POST /deals/{id}/issues Report a delivery issue GET /deals/{id}/escrow Escrow state ({ "onchain": false } when off) GET /approvals, POST /approvals/{id}/decide Human approvals

docs.title: Fee quote
docs.text:
Draft fee schedule 2026-10-24.1 is implemented, not final, and subject to change. Total contract value and term select the rate; it applies to cycle gross. Renewals use 75% of the rate, then the $5 minimum fee applies. The quote function rejects cycles below $25. Final pricing is not yet published. Development quotes are not a published pricing commitment. The fee-quote route is GET /api/v1/fees/quote:

curl "https://api.example/api/v1/fees/quote?contract_value_usd=5000&term_days=60"

Parameters: contract_value_usd (required), term_days or term_months (one required), renewal (true/false), cycle_amount_usd. The response includes fee_usd and seller_net_usd. See Paying.

docs.title: Listings
docs.text: A listing is a seller's offer of capacity. Creating one produces a draft; tier and reliability are derived by the server, never typed by the seller. A draft goes live after the machine is measured and you call revalidate.

docs.title: Create a listing
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/listings/create (identical to POST /api/v1/listings). REST and the MCP post_listing / create_listing tools share one schema.

Field Type Notes capability object Required. Validated by the engine. title string 1–160 characters. notes string Optional, up to 4,000 characters. Contact details are stripped from public views. 
curl -X POST https://api.example/api/v1/listings/create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: rack-01-listing" \
  -d @listing.json

listing.json (this is the shape used in Pewter's own tests):

{
  "title": "8x H100 rack",
  "notes": "demo",
  "capability": {
    "schema_version": "1",
    "kind": "gpu",
    "gpu": { "model": "H100", "canonical": "H100", "vram_gb": 80, "count_per_node": 8, "nodes": 1, "intra": "nvlink", "inter": "ib_400g" },
    "network": { "up_mbps": 10000, "down_mbps": 10000, "class": "datacenter", "public_ip": true },
    "region": { "country": "US" },
    "availability": { "from": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z", "until": null, "schedule": "24x7", "min_hours": 1 },
    "price": { "unit": "gpu_hr", "amount_usd": 2, "negotiable": false },
    "contract_type": "rental"
  }
}

Response 201:

{ "data": { "id": "LST-…", "status": "draft", "title": "8x H100 rack", "capability": { "…": "…" }, "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…" } }

Sending the request without a token returns 401. Replaying the same Idempotency-Key returns the same listing.

docs.title: Other listing routes
docs.text: Method & path Purpose GET /listings Your own listings (opt-in paging). POST /listings/{id}/revalidate Ask Pewter to validate the listing against the machine's measurements. GET /listings/{id}/verification Validation state. GET /listings/{id}/node Machine linked to the listing. POST /listings/{id}/maintenance Announce maintenance. POST /listings/{id}/drain Stop taking new work. GET /capacity Other sellers' live capacity, anonymous (seller_ref, your own rows flagged is_own: true). Query: kind, gpu, region, max_price, verification_min (S0–S3), limit, cursor.

docs.title: Pairing a machine
docs.text:
1. POST /api/v1/nodes/pairings with { "listing_id": "LST-…" } returns a pairing code. Codes expire after 10 minutes; at most 5 open codes per listing.
  2. The agent calls POST /api/v1/nodes/register. This route is public but must be signed by the key being registered and needs a live pairing code.
  3. The agent sends POST /api/v1/nodes/{id}/heartbeat every 60 seconds, signed with the machine's key. Measurements arrive only in these signed requests and are never seller-typed.

Other routes: GET /nodes, GET /nodes/{id}, POST /nodes/{id}/edge-verdict (signed verdict from the edge verifier).

docs.title: Whole GPUs and slices
docs.text:
Whole GPU Slice What A full physical device Part of a device Supported NVIDIA, AMD NVIDIA MIG only, from a known profile Not supported — AMD compute/memory partitions that share the driver interface; self-certified slices

Overlapping device ranges are refused.

docs.title: Metering
docs.text:
• Each heartbeat credits the gap between two heartbeats for every allocated device.
  • Presence follows the allocated device id, not a device index.
  • A health sensor the driver did not report counts as unknown, not healthy.
  • Usage rolls up into hourly tranches; per-delivery slices are available at GET /deals/{id}/delivery/slices.

docs.title: Regions & sanctions (OFAC)
docs.text:
Pewter follows U.S. OFAC sanctions rules. In plain terms:

Blocked everywhere (comprehensive programs): Cuba, Iran, North Korea, the Crimea region of Ukraine (including Sevastopol), and the so-called Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics. Because region codes can't draw the exact legal line, the whole Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts are blocked, and a Ukrainian location without a region is blocked.

Not blocked as whole countries (selective programs): for example Russia, Belarus, China, Venezuela, Burma and Syria. For these, specific people and companies are screened by name against the official sanctions list when you register a machine, create a listing, pair a machine, or create a deal.

Fail-closed. If the location check is missing, or the policy or sanctions snapshot is out of date, the request is denied rather than allowed. Country headers sent by the caller are ignored.

Note

Location comes from IP geolocation, which is a control, not a guarantee. This page is not legal advice. The policy is versioned and reviewed against the official OFAC pages on a schedule.

docs.title: Buyer CLI
docs.text:
The public Pewter CLI is pewter (alias pew), version 0.1.0. It is read-only. It talks only to the Pewter staging API and refuses production, including api.omegacompute.com. Account calls use a permissioned pck_ API key, minted only after someone who already has a Pewter account approves a device login in the Pewter app.

HEIR PTE. LTD., trading as Omega Compute, publishes the signed release from OmegaComputes/pewter.

pewter is not pewt. The Python package pewt 0.1.1 is a library and a pewt command for the orchestration API. It does not log in. This page is only the pewter / pew CLI.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
On macOS (the supported Mac install; darwin binaries in 0.1.0 are not notarized):

brew trust --formula omegacomputes/tap/pewter   # Homebrew 7; required before the formula will load
brew install omegacomputes/tap/pewter

On Linux, and on macOS once OpenSSL 3 is first on PATH:

curl -fsSL https://omegacompute.com/install | sh

Prefer to read the installer first?

curl -fsSLo install.sh https://omegacompute.com/install && less install.sh && sh install.sh

Both commands install pewter and the pew alias. Options on the curl installer include --version X.Y.Z, --dir DIR, --dry-run (verify only) and --verbose.

docs.title: Verify the signature
docs.text:
The curl installer downloads the archive from https://omegacompute.com/cli/, checks an Ed25519 signature on SHA256SUMS with a public key built into the installer, then checks the SHA-256 of the archive against that list. If the signature, the checksum, or the archive contents fail, nothing is installed.

The same public key is in the CLI README and at https://omegacompute.com/cli/pewter-release.pub, so you can compare them. To verify without installing:

curl -fsSLo install.sh https://omegacompute.com/install && less install.sh && sh install.sh --dry-run

That should end with Dry run: pewter v0.1.0 verified. Nothing was installed.

Homebrew does not check the Ed25519 signature itself. The formula pins the SHA-256 of each archive, copied from SHA256SUMS only after that signature was verified.

docs.title: Sign in and the staging host
docs.text:
Public sign-up is not open. You need an existing Pewter app account.

pewter login

The command prints a device URL and a short code on stderr. Open the URL, enter the code, and approve the request in the Pewter app. That mints a pck_ CLI credential: hashed on the server, scoped, revocable, with a 90-day life. The access token is stored locally and is never printed. The CLI accepts only pck_ keys. It refuses omk_ agent keys and session tokens, and it will not store them.

pewter --version
pewter status
pewter whoami

pewter --version should report 0.1.0. pewter status can run with no key and should show the staging host as healthy. pewter instruments is a public catalog and also needs no key. pewter whoami without a key exits 3.

The default API is:

https://pewter-staging-production.up.railway.app/api/v1

That host is the staging orchestration. Account data there is not the live book. Loopback is allowed for tests. Any other host, including https://api.omegacompute.com/api/v1, is a hard error (exit 2). Production is not enabled in this release.

pewter logout revokes the credential on the server, then deletes the local copy.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Available in v0.1.0: login, logout, whoami, status, instruments, listings, orders, balance, verify, version, completion.

connect, pay, and the seller agent are not part of this release. Buyers who need HTTP or an assistant integration can still use the API or the MCP server. Those paths use engine agent keys (omk_), which the public CLI will not store.

docs.title: Buyer flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A[Sign in / agent key] --> B[Browse capacity<br/>GET /capacity]
  B --> C[Quote and order<br/>POST /orders/quote, /orders]
  C --> D[Match becomes a deal]
  D --> E[Agree terms<br/>POST /deals/id/terms, /accept]
  E --> F[Human approval if required]
  F --> G[Submit jobs<br/>POST /deals/id/jobs]
  G --> H[Logs and artifacts]
  H --> I[Delivery metered hourly]
  1. Browse live capacity (anonymous seller references) by GPU, region, price and verification tier.
  2. Quote and order, or post a need/RFQ and let matching find sellers.
  3. Agree terms. A deal is non-binding until both sides accept and any required human approval clears.
  4. Run jobs — containers on NVIDIA/AMD machines; mlx, pytorch-mps or llama.cpp on Apple silicon. Read logs and artifacts, cancel any time.
  5. Problems? Report a delivery issue; replacement hosts can be approved.

docs.title: Getting connected
docs.text:
Step Status Join the waitlist (POST /api/v1/waitlist) Available Public self-serve sign-up Coming soon — accounts are invite-only today Sign in with Apple, Google, or device code (/api/v1/auth/*) Built Onboarding questionnaire (/api/v1/onboarding/*, or MCP get_onboarding_questionnaire) Built; you can skip it Create an agent key (POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/keys) Built — shown once, store it safely Connect an assistant over MCP Built — see MCP Pair a machine (sellers) Built — see Seller flow

Revoke a credential with POST /api/v1/auth/credentials/{id}/revoke.

docs.title: Paying and payouts
docs.text:
Not live

No real-money payment path is switched on. What exists today runs in test or sandbox modes, and final pricing is not yet published.

docs.title: What's built
docs.text:
• Card checkout through Stripe, test mode only (it refuses to run with a live key).
  • On-chain escrow for a deal, reported by GET /deals/{id}/escrow — tested on a public testnet only; { "onchain": false } when off.
  • Internal ledger. A double-entry sandbox ledger tracks gross, fee, holdback, seller net and refunds per hourly tranche. It is an internal record, not legal escrow.
  • Holdback. Part of each tranche can be held back for a period after delivery before release.
  • Seller-paid fee. Buyers pay the listed price; the platform fee is taken from the seller's side.

docs.title: Draft fee schedule (2026-10-24.1), not final, subject to change
docs.text:
This is the implemented development schedule, not a final pricing commitment. Fees are seller-paid. The total contract value selects the band; the rate applies to each cycle's gross amount.

Total contract value (USD) Less than 30 days 1–6 months More than 6 months $25 to < $2,500 15% 12% 10% $2,500 to < $25,000 12% 10% 8% $25,000 to < $250,000 9% 7% 6% $250,000 to < $2,500,000 6% 5% 4% $2,500,000 and above 4% 3% 2.5%
  • Lower band boundaries are inclusive. No deals below $25 per cycle are accepted by the fee-quote function.
  • When specified in days, exactly 30 through 183 days use the middle column; more than 183 days uses the last column. The 183-day interpretation of six months is an open assumption. When specified in months, 1 through 6 months use the middle column. If both are supplied, months takes precedence.
  • Renewals through Omega use 75% of the band rate (a 25% rate discount), then a $5 minimum fee applies per cycle. The same $5 minimum applies to non-renewals. A cycle cannot exceed total contract value.
  • The highest band returns negotiated: true; the rates above are the code's default calculation, not a negotiated offer.
  • Calculation uses integer micro-USD and rounds half up. The internal sandbox rate-lock helper does not enforce the quote function's cycle floor or minimum fee; do not treat sandbox tranche behavior as a final commercial quote.

For example, a $5,000 contract lasting 60 days with a $1,000 cycle has a 10% rate: $100 fee and $900 seller net. A renewal at the same values has a 7.5% rate: $75 fee and $925 seller net.

The fee-quote route is GET /api/v1/fees/quote. See Deals, orders & fees for parameters. Final pricing is not yet published.

docs.title: Seller flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A[Sign in] --> B[Create draft listing<br/>POST /listings/create]
  B --> C[Pairing code<br/>POST /nodes/pairings]
  C --> D[pewter-node-agent up --code]
  D --> E[Signed measurement + heartbeats]
  E --> F[POST /listings/id/revalidate]
  F --> G[Listing live]
  G --> H[Buyer deal accepted]
  H --> I[Jobs run on your machine]
  I --> J[Hourly tranches metered]
  J --> K[Payout after holdback]
  1. Create a draft listing. Describe the GPUs, network, region, availability and price (Listings).
  2. Pair the machine with a code (valid 10 minutes) and run the agent (Commands).
  3. Measurement. The agent reads the GPUs and signs what it saw; declarations alone never make a listing live.
  4. Revalidate. The listing becomes live once measurement backs it.
  5. Serve deals. Accept terms, run buyers' jobs, keep heartbeating. Use maintenance or drain when you need downtime.
  6. Get paid. See Paying.

docs.title: Verified badge
docs.text:
Verified means Pewter has proven that the GPU itself holds the claimed compute and memory — not just that the machine reported it.

Currently OFF for every machine

Verified is switched off and fails closed. No listing shows it today. A passing proof does not set it, and nothing a seller sends can set it.

It stays off until:

  • the GPU proof workload has run on real hardware,
  • timing calibration is done, and
  • remote checks can show the memory actually sits on the named GPU.

Listings still carry a verification tier (S0–S3) based on measurements; buyers can filter with verification_min. See Proofs.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
Pewter runs a Model Context Protocol server so assistants and agents can browse capacity, manage listings, pair machines and run jobs with the same rules as the REST API.

  • Endpoint: https://api.example/api/v1/mcp (HTTP). Client-specific profiles live at /api/v1/mcp/claude and /api/v1/mcp/chatgpt.
  • One server, filtered per caller. An omk_ agent key sees every tool. A sign-in token sees only the tools its scopes allow, further capped by the profile it was issued for.
  • No tool moves money. Payments, wallet and account management are app-only.

docs.title: Signing in from an assistant (OAuth)
docs.text:
Assistants that support MCP sign-in discover Pewter through standard OAuth metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, then send you to a Pewter page to approve or decline.

  • Approved clients only. A client's redirect address must be on Pewter's allowlist: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code callbacks, plus approved loopback callbacks for local tools. Anything else is refused.
  • Client ID metadata documents. A client may identify itself with an HTTPS URL that serves its metadata. Pewter fetches it with strict guards: HTTPS on the default port only, a host name (not an IP), no private or loopback destinations, no redirects, a 5-second timeout and an 8 KB cap. The host is resolved twice and the connection is pinned to the address that was checked, so a DNS-rebinding answer is refused.
  • Grants can be listed and revoked (/api/v1/oauth/grants).

docs.title: Connecting a client
Example tool call
docs.text:
A raw JSON-RPC call (what your client sends for you):

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "post_listing",
    "arguments": { "capability": { "schema_version": "1", "kind": "gpu", "…": "…" }, "title": "8x H100 rack", "idempotency_key": "mcp-create-1" }
  }
}

Replaying the same idempotency_key returns the original listing. A token without the listing scope is refused.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does get_profile Get account profile get_onboarding_questionnaire, answer_compat_questions Onboarding questions resolve_requirements Turn a job description into requirements list_capacity Browse available capacity post_listing / create_listing Create a capacity listing (draft) update_listing, retire_listing, list_my_listings Manage listings get_validation_status, request_revalidation Listing validation create_pairing_code, list_machines, get_node_status, disconnect_machine Machines get_delivery_status, list_tranches, get_tranche, report_delivery_issue, approve_reprovision Delivery submit_job, list_jobs, get_job_logs, cancel_job Jobs on a deal announce_maintenance, drain_listing Seller operations get_username, set_username Username get_referral_code, claim_referral_code, list_referral_rewards, get_referral_terms Referrals

Which tools you see depends on your key or sign-in scopes.

docs.title: Open source plans
docs.text:
Pewter's code is private today. We are preparing for an eventual open source release. These pages describe how we intend to work once repositories are public:

  • Contributing
  • Code of conduct
  • Security policy
  • License recommendation — Apache-2.0 is recommended; no license has been applied yet.
  • Support

docs.title: Code of conduct
docs.text: Local preparation draft: we are preparing for an eventual open source release. Contributor Covenant 2.1; enforcement contact: hello@omegacompute.com.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at hello@omegacompute.com. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: Attribution
docs.text:
This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html.

Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder.

For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see the FAQ at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq. Translations are available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: We are preparing for an eventual open source release. These guidelines are a local draft for invited collaborators; they do not grant access, publish code, or offer a license.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Read the repository README and Code of conduct. Agree on the problem and acceptance criteria with a maintainer before undertaking a large change. Use the relevant repository's documented setup commands; ask if they are missing. Do not infer production readiness from a local test result.

docs.title: A useful change
docs.text:
1. Work on a focused branch, not directly on the default branch.
  2. Explain the problem, proposed behavior, and any compatibility or security implications.
  3. Add or update tests and documentation. Run the repository's documented checks and report exact commands and outcomes, including skipped checks.
  4. Open a pull request with a small, reviewable diff. Include a rollback approach where behavior changes.
  5. Wait for maintainer review. Publishing, deploying, changing verification policy, and releasing funds are separate approvals, not consequences of a merged patch.

Never commit secrets, personal data, production dumps, or unredacted logs. Do not enable Verified or represent compute or allocation checks as proof of hardware residency. Follow Security policy for suspected vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Contribution rights — decision pending
docs.text:
We recommend the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) rather than a separate contributor license agreement. This is a proposal, not an active submission requirement. If adopted at launch, contributors must review https://developercertificate.org/ and use git commit -s only when they can truthfully certify the contribution. A sign-off is not a cryptographic commit signature.

No license is applied by this document. See License recommendation. Questions: hello@omegacompute.com.

docs.title: License recommendation — decision record draft
docs.text: We are preparing for an eventual open source release. No license is granted or applied by this document. Do not copy license text into private repositories as part of preparation.

docs.title: Recommendation: Apache License 2.0
docs.text:
Apache-2.0 is an OSI-approved permissive license with an explicit contributor patent grant and patent-termination provisions. Its familiar terms suit enterprise adoption while allowing commercial use and modification. Its notice and attribution obligations need to be preserved. It is a good default for the planned engine and node agent, subject to ownership and dependency review.

MIT is a simpler permissive alternative, but does not express the same explicit patent grant. Choose it only after weighing that trade-off. Existing repositories may have their own licenses; inventory those rather than overwriting them. A repository may need a different decision because of third-party obligations.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: Recommend DCO sign-off, not a CLA, as the initial contribution-rights process. DCO is a provenance certification, not a substitute for a project license or rights audit. Confirm copyright ownership, employer permissions, and any contractor agreements before adopting it. Counsel should review patent and contribution-rights questions.

docs.title: Before any repository goes public
docs.text:
• Approve exact release scope and license with the rights holders.
  • Audit direct and transitive dependencies, vendored code, copied snippets, datasets, fonts, images, and brand assets; record licenses and required notices in an inventory/SBOM.
  • Check copyleft compatibility and any redistribution restrictions; prepare NOTICE/attribution files where required.
  • Scan the entire Git history and all publishable branches/tags for secrets, personal data, customer information, and private infrastructure. Rotate exposed secrets; deletion alone is not remediation.
  • Review workflows, release artifacts, package metadata, and deployment hooks for accidental publication or production access.
  • Approve supported versions, maintainers, vulnerability intake, and release gates.
  • Only after explicit launch approval, add the selected LICENSE and notices to the approved release branches. Do not change visibility automatically.

References: https://opensource.org/license/apache-2-0 · https://opensource.org/license/mit · https://developercertificate.org/

docs.title: Security policy — preparation draft
docs.text: We are preparing for an eventual open source release. This local draft does not announce a public security program.

docs.title: Private disclosure
docs.text:
Please send suspected vulnerabilities to hello@omegacompute.com. A dedicated security mailbox has not been verified, so do not rely on security@omegacompute.com. Mailbox monitoring and an escalation owner must be confirmed before launch.

Do not disclose vulnerabilities in public issues, discussions, or pull requests. Include the affected component and version or commit, impact, minimal reproduction steps, and redacted supporting evidence. Never email passwords, tokens, private keys, personal data, or live exploit payloads. Ask for a secure transfer method if sensitive evidence is necessary.

Test only systems you own or have explicit authorization to assess. Do not access other users' workloads, interrupt service, move funds, or perform destructive tests. This policy does not confer testing authorization or legal safe harbor.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
TBD. No supported-version matrix or response-time commitment has been approved. Before launch, maintainers must name supported releases, triage owners, and a disclosure-coordination process. Coordinate publication with maintainers so fixes can be prepared without exposing users.

There is no announced bug bounty or reward promise. Private vulnerability reporting through GitHub should be enabled per public repository at launch if available and staffed.

docs.title: Python SDK (pewt)
docs.text:
pewt 0.1.1 is the buyer-side Python client and CLI for the Pewter orchestration API. It lists anonymous GPU capacity, requests an advisory quote, places and cancels orders, reads deals, and submits jobs on Test network deals. It can sign a Base Sepolia USDC payment for the paid capacity read. Version 0.1.1 does not log in, and it does not wrap seller, node, or escrow writes.

This is not the public pewter CLI (alias pew, v0.1.0). pewter is a separate binary. pewt is the Python package: a library plus the pewt command.

The library speaks SI workloads in plain language: you name the GPU, the count, and the hours. A capacity row does not carry a supplier identity. Rows carry seller_ref (an anonymous alias) and is_own.

Apache-2.0. HEIR PTE. LTD. trading as Omega Compute.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Python 3.9 or newer. The package classifiers list 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.

pip install pewt

The console script is pewt. python -m pewt runs the same CLI: __main__ calls pewt.cli:main.

pewt.__version__ is 0.1.1.

docs.title: Auth and host
docs.text:
Point at staging

The library default is production https://api.omegacompute.com/api/v1 (PRODUCTION_API_BASE). Set PEWTER_API_URL or base_url= until you are ready. Every example on this page uses staging.

Staging is STAGING_API_BASE:

https://pewter-staging-production.up.railway.app/api/v1

export PEWTER_API_URL=https://pewter-staging-production.up.railway.app/api/v1
export PEWTER_API_KEY

PEWTER_API_KEY is sent as Authorization: Bearer on calls that require a key. Keys are omk_ (agent), pws_ (human session), or pck_ (CLI). Pass api_key= to the constructor to override the environment variable. Do not put a key in source.

base_url= overrides PEWTER_API_URL. The CLI flag is --base-url. timeout on the constructor, and --timeout on the CLI, default to 30 seconds.

GET /health and GET /instruments do not send the key. The x402 helper does not send it either. It uses a separate Base Sepolia signing key, described below.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
from pewt import Client, STAGING_API_BASE

client = Client(base_url=STAGING_API_BASE)  # PEWTER_API_KEY from the environment
client.health()
offers = client.offers.list(gpu="H100", region="US")
quote = client.orders.quote(
    side="bid",
    instrument_id="gpu:H100:od:US:now",
    price_usd_per_unit=2.0,
    gpus=1,
    hours=1,
)
hours = client.hours.get()
jobs = client.jobs.list(deal_id="DEAL-...")
job = client.jobs.submit(
    deal_id="DEAL-...",
    runtime="container",
    image="python:3.12-slim",
    command=["python", "-c", "print(1)"],
    time_limit_s=60,
)
client.jobs.cancel(job.id)
client.close()

price_usd_per_unit=2.0 is the limit the caller sends. It is not a published index.

Client is also a context manager. with Client(base_url=STAGING_API_BASE) as client calls close() on the way out. Closing twice is safe. A closed client raises PewterError with code="closed".

docs.title: AsyncClient
docs.text:
AsyncClient has the same methods as coroutines. async with calls aclose().

import asyncio
from pewt import AsyncClient, STAGING_API_BASE

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(base_url=STAGING_API_BASE) as client:
        offers = await client.offers.list(gpu="H100", region="US")
        print(len(offers))

asyncio.run(main())

await client.aclose() closes without async with. Closing twice is safe.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Successful engine calls arrive as { "data": ... }. The client unwraps data. List routes return a bare array unless you pass limit and/or cursor, in which case the result is a Page: items, next_cursor, and total. limit is an integer from 1 to 200. GET /health is not wrapped; client.health() reads it directly.

Writes other than the advisory quote send Idempotency-Key (1–80 characters). If you omit idempotency_key=, the client generates a UUID4. Send the same key again to replay the original result. POST /orders/quote does not send the header.

docs.title: Offers
docs.text:
client.offers.list calls GET /capacity.

Filters: kind, gpu, region, max_price, verification_min (S0, S1, S2, S3), plus limit and cursor. max_price, when set, must be a finite USD amount greater than 0 and at most 1000. Each row is an Offer: GPU model, VRAM, region, USD price per gpu_hr, assurance tier, listing id, seller_ref, and is_own. The manufacturer GPU name is the model, such as H100 or RTX 4090. The row does not include a supplier name, email, phone, or company.

page = client.offers.list(gpu="H100", region="US", verification_min="S1", limit=20)
page.items
page.next_cursor
page.total

docs.title: Instruments
docs.text:
client.instruments.list calls GET /instruments and does not send a key.

Filters: gpu, term, region, limit, cursor. Each row is an Instrument. Useful instrument ids look like gpu:H100:od:US:now.

docs.title: Orders
docs.text:
There is no separate job-quote route. A quote is POST /orders/quote. A job runs on a Test network deal after an order matches.

orders.quote and orders.create take the same order fields. client_order_id is optional on a quote and required on create. idempotency_key applies to create only.

Argument Required Values side yes bid or ask instrument_id yes price_usd_per_unit yes Caller limit. Finite, greater than 0, at most 1000. Not a published index. gpus yes hours yes client_order_id create only At most 80 characters firmness no firm or indicative min_fill_gpus no all_or_none no Boolean time_in_force no GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK expires_at no contract_type no rental or purchase book no live or sandbox listing_id no seller_verification_min no S0–S3 residency no List of strings interconnect no network_class no List of datacenter, colo, residential country no idempotency_key no Create only. 1–80 characters.

The order argument is seller_verification_min. Offer search uses verification_min on offers.list. Those names are not interchangeable.

created = client.orders.create(
    client_order_id="bid-100",
    side="bid",
    instrument_id="gpu:H100:od:US:now",
    price_usd_per_unit=2.0,
    gpus=1,
    hours=1,
    book="sandbox",
)
created.http_status  # 201, or 202 when the order is pending_approval
client.orders.get(created.order.id)
client.orders.cancel(created.order.id)

orders.create returns the order, any deals, and http_status. orders.get returns the order and deal_ids. orders.cancel returns the order. Pass idempotency_key= to cancel when you want to choose the key.

orders.list filters are status, side (bid or ask), instrument_id, limit, and cursor.

docs.title: Deals
docs.text:
client.deals.list takes limit and cursor. Omit both for the array of Deal rows. client.deals.get(deal_id) returns one Deal.

client.deals.list()
client.deals.get("DEAL-...")

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
Jobs are buyer-submitted and run on Test network deals only. The server enforces that.

client.jobs.list(deal_id) returns the jobs for that deal: jobs, can_submit, stop_reason, gpu_s_used, gpu_s_billable, and gpu_s_included. It does not take limit or cursor.

client.jobs.submit(deal_id, *, runtime, command, time_limit_s, ...) returns a Job. Runtimes: container, mlx, pytorch-mps, llama.cpp.

A container job needs an image such as python:3.12-slim. Native runtimes take no image. The first command token is python for mlx and pytorch-mps, and llama-cli, llama-completion, or llama-bench for llama.cpp. command is a list of 1 to 64 strings.

env names are UPPER_SNAKE and must not start with PEWTER_. At most 32 variables. files are objects with name and content. Names are plain names (no paths), at most 8. Each content string is at most 64 KB, and the files together are at most 128 KB. time_limit_s is 10–86400. gpus, when set, is 1–64. idempotency_key is optional.

job = client.jobs.submit(
    deal_id="DEAL-...",
    runtime="mlx",
    command=["python", "-c", "print(1)"],
    time_limit_s=60,
    env={"MODEL_NAME": "demo"},
)
client.jobs.get(job.id)

client.jobs.cancel(job_id) returns the Job. A running cancel stops at the machine's next heartbeat. Pass idempotency_key= to choose the key.

logs = client.jobs.logs(job.id, after=0)
while not logs.done:
    logs = client.jobs.logs(job.id, after=logs.next)
names = client.jobs.artifacts(job.id)
one = client.jobs.artifacts(job.id, name="out.txt")

jobs.logs takes optional after (integer ≥ 0) and limit (1–1000). Poll with the returned next value until done is true. jobs.artifacts lists artifacts, or returns one artifact when name is set. A blank name is rejected.

docs.title: Hours and identity
docs.text:
client.hours.get() calls GET /hours. unit is gpu_hours. The summary has active, negotiating, closed, and all-time counts. by_role has a buyer bucket and a seller bucket (by_role["buyer"], by_role["seller"]).

client.me.get() calls GET /me.

client.health() calls GET /health. It is unauthenticated liveness. The body is not a data envelope. A Health value has status, api_version, time, and uptime_s.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
HTTP errors are not swallowed. Failures raise PewterError with status, code, message, request_id, and details. Timeouts raise PewterError with code="timeout". Connection failures use code="transport_error". Redirects are refused (code="redirect") and are not followed. A closed client raises code="closed".

from pewt import Client, PewterError, STAGING_API_BASE

with Client(base_url=STAGING_API_BASE) as client:
    try:
        client.orders.get("ORD-...")
    except PewterError as exc:
        print(exc.status, exc.code, exc.message, exc.request_id, exc.details)

X402Error is a PewterError for a refused payment requirement or a lingering HTTP 402. X402ConfigError is an X402Error raised when the Base Sepolia signing key is missing or is not a 32-byte hex key. except PewterError catches both.

docs.title: x402 on Base Sepolia
docs.text:
client.x402.capacity(...) calls GET /api/v1/x402/capacity (same filters and rows as offers.list). An unpaid request is HTTP 402. The helper checks the requirement, signs an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, and retries once with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.

This is Test network only. The helper does not send PEWTER_API_KEY.

  • Chain: Base Sepolia, CAIP eip155:84532, chain id 84532.
  • Asset: Circle USDC 0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e (name USDC, version 2, 6 decimals).
  • The helper refuses Base mainnet (chain id 8453), mainnet USDC 0x833589fCD6eBd6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, and the Pewter staging test token 0xd4822Fa535d1784F880969f0E7Ef5c3A209CdF20 (no EIP-3009).
  • It pays the amount in the 402, and refuses anything above 1 USDC.
  • The signing key comes from PEWTER_X402_TEST_PRIVATE_KEY or x402_private_key=. There is no default wallet. The key is never logged. The server settles; this client does not call the facilitator.
from pewt import Client, STAGING_API_BASE

client = Client(base_url=STAGING_API_BASE)
rows = client.x402.capacity(gpu="H100")
result = client.x402.call_tool("list_capacity", {"gpu": "H100"})
client.close()

call_tool posts one JSON-RPC tools/call and returns that object. It does not unwrap a data envelope. Names are limited to list_capacity, resolve_requirements, get_quotes, get_market_summary, and get_price_history. Any other name is refused locally, including writes and account tools. An optional request_id= defaults to 1. Offer search for buyers stays on offers.list.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Global flags: --base-url and --timeout (seconds, default 30). When --base-url and PEWTER_API_URL are both unset, the CLI uses the production library default. Point it at staging.

export PEWTER_API_URL=https://pewter-staging-production.up.railway.app/api/v1
export PEWTER_API_KEY

pewt --base-url "$PEWTER_API_URL" status
pewt offers --gpu H100 --region US --verification-min S1
pewt instruments --gpu H100 --limit 5
pewt quote --side bid --instrument-id gpu:H100:od:US:now --price 2 --gpus 1 --hours 1
pewt orders create --client-order-id bid-100 --side bid --instrument-id gpu:H100:od:US:now --price 2 --gpus 1 --hours 1 --book sandbox
pewt orders list --side bid
pewt deals list
pewt jobs --deal DEAL-...
pewt jobs submit --deal DEAL-... --runtime container --image python:3.12-slim \
  --command python --command=-c --command 'print(1)' --time-limit 60
pewt jobs logs JOB-...
pewt jobs cancel JOB-...
pewt hours
pewt whoami

--price is the caller limit (price_usd_per_unit), not a published index. The 2 above is that limit.

pewt offers prints the manufacturer GPU name, count, VRAM, country or region, USD price per GPU-hour, verification tier, listing id, seller_ref, and is_own. It does not print a supplier name, email, phone, or company.

pewt status prints the configured host and health. pewt whoami is GET /me. pewt hours prints unit (gpu_hours) and the active, negotiating, closed, and all-time figures, including buyer and seller totals. pewt instruments needs no API key.

Commands and flags:

Command Flags offers --kind, --gpu, --region, --max-price, --verification-min (S0–S3), --limit, --cursor instruments --gpu, --term, --region, --limit, --cursor status none whoami none hours none quote Order flags below. --client-order-id is optional. No idempotency flag. orders list --status, --side (bid or ask), --instrument-id, --limit, --cursor orders get order_id (id or client_order_id) orders cancel order_id, --idempotency-key orders create --client-order-id (required) and the order flags below, plus --idempotency-key deals list --limit, --cursor deals get deal_id jobs --deal lists jobs when no subcommand is given jobs list --deal (required) jobs get job_id jobs submit --deal, --runtime (container, mlx, pytorch-mps, llama.cpp), repeated --command, --time-limit, optional --image, --gpus, repeated --env NAME=VALUE, repeated --file name=local-path, --idempotency-key jobs cancel job_id, --idempotency-key jobs logs job_id, --after, --limit jobs artifacts job_id, --name

pewt orders and pewt deals need a subcommand. pewt jobs needs --deal or a subcommand (list, get, submit, cancel, logs, artifacts).

Order flags on quote and orders create: --side, --instrument-id, --price, --gpus, --hours, --firmness (firm or indicative), --min-fill-gpus, --all-or-none, --time-in-force (GTC, GTD, IOC, FOK), --expires-at, --contract-type (rental or purchase), --book (live or sandbox), --listing-id, --verification-min (S0–S3), repeated --residency, --interconnect, repeated --network-class (datacenter, colo, or residential), --country. --verification-min on these commands is seller_verification_min. On offers the same flag is the capacity filter verification_min.

--all-or-none is a switch. Omit it to leave the field unset. Repeat --command once per token. A token that starts with a dash is --command=-c. --image is required for container and forbidden for native runtimes. --file reads a local UTF-8 file. The name on the left of = is a plain file name, with no directory.

--limit and --cursor opt into a page. Omit both for the legacy array. Commands that page are offers, instruments, orders list, and deals list.

docs.title: Names you can import
docs.text: AsyncClient, Client, Deal, Health, HoursSummary, Instrument, Job, Offer, Order, PRODUCTION_API_BASE, Page, PewterError, Quote, STAGING_API_BASE, X402ConfigError, X402Error, and __version__.

docs.title: Seller agent
docs.text: pewter-node-agent (also installed as pewter-node) runs on the seller's machine. It pairs the machine with a listing, measures its GPUs, sends signed heartbeats, answers capacity proofs through the edge verifier, and runs buyers' jobs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Node.js 22.18 or newer
  • NVIDIA (nvidia-smi) or AMD (amd-smi / rocm-smi) drivers, or a Mac with Apple silicon
  • Docker for container jobs on NVIDIA/AMD machines. On a Mac, run the agent natively — Docker cannot reach Apple GPUs.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
A published package or installer is coming soon. Today the agent runs from its source folder:

node src/cli.ts version

A Docker image definition exists in the source; a published image is not yet available.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Purpose PEWTER_PAIRING_CODE Pairing code (same as --code) PEWTER_API_URL API base, ending in /api/v1 PEWTER_NODE_NAME Machine name (same as --name) PEWTER_NODE_DIR Where the agent keeps its key and state PEWTER_NODE_BENCH=0 Skip the benchmark PEWTER_JOBS=0 Don't accept jobs PEWTER_EDGE_WORKLOAD=cuda Run the real GPU proof workload (no CPU fallback)

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
pewter-node-agent up [--code XXXX-XXXX] [--api URL] [--name NAME]
pewter-node-agent status | measure | down | install-service | uninstall-service | version

pewter-node-agent node up works too.

Command What it does up Pairs on first run (needs --code), then heartbeats every 60 s until Ctrl-C. Prints Paired as NOD-… for listing LST-…. status Shows node id, listing id, name, API, last measurement, heartbeats sent and supplier score — or Not paired. measure Measures the GPUs now and prints the result as JSON. down Disconnects this machine from Pewter. install-service macOS only: installs a launchd agent so it starts at login and restarts if it stops. Pair first. On Linux use Docker or a systemd unit. uninstall-service Removes the launchd agent. version Prints the version.

docs.title: GPU detection
docs.text:
Vendor Read from Notes NVIDIA nvidia-smi Whole GPUs and MIG slices with a known profile. AMD amd-smi / rocm-smi Whole GPUs only. Partition modes (SPX/DPX/TPX/QPX/CPX, NPS) are recorded but are not isolation. Render nodes are mapped from PCI inventory. Apple silicon ioreg GPU cores and unified memory. Jobs run natively (mlx, pytorch-mps, llama.cpp), not in Docker.

Each GPU reports model, memory, device class (whole, mig, vgpu, sriov, AMD partitions…), isolation, a hashed identity, and health (XID, ECC, RAS, exclusive mode). Only sensors the driver actually printed count; anything absent stays unknown.

docs.title: Proofs & the edge verifier
docs.text: Pewter asks a machine to prove capacity rather than trusting what it reports.

docs.title: Compute check
docs.text: The machine multiplies two challenge matrices over the prime field p = 2³¹ − 1 and commits to a Merkle root of every result row before seeing the challenge. The verifier opens the rows, recomputes the result, and runs two independent Freivalds rounds. A wrong result slips through with probability below 2⁻⁴⁰ (less than one in a trillion). A list of sampled rows is not accepted as proof.

docs.title: Memory check
docs.text: A commit-then-open check: the machine commits to chunks filling the claimed memory (minus a 512 MiB reserve), then opens the chunks the verifier picks.

docs.title: Edge verifier
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Seller agent
  participant P as Pewter API
  participant E as Edge verifier
  A->>P: signed heartbeat
  P-->>A: signed grant naming the agent's certificate
  A->>E: connect (mutual TLS) + grant
  A->>E: commit (Merkle roots)
  E-->>A: challenge
  A->>E: openings
  E->>E: recompute rows, Freivalds x2, memory openings
  E->>P: signed one-use verdict
  P->>P: check signature, re-run transcript
  Note over P: Verified stays OFF

What this does not prove yet

Remote timing can't yet prove the memory sits on that GPU, the GPU proof workload hasn't been validated on real hardware, and timing calibration isn't done. Until then a passing verdict never sets Verified. A CPU test workload is the default and can never become a production verdict.
